memory_update.text: POWL has the clearest company-disclosed AI/data-center power evidence in this node via a >$400 million data-center electrical order and record backlog, but its market cap has expanded into large-cap territory and attention is rising.

IESC is a strong underfollowed electrical-infrastructure candidate: data-center demand is explicitly driving Communications and Infrastructure Solutions growth, but the company is now large-cap and needs customer/backlog mix verification.

MYRG maps to the transmission, distribution, substation, and electrical-construction layer of the AI power bottleneck; strongest next check is project geography/customer linkage to data-center load clusters.

ATKR is a lower-confidence second-order candidate in conduit/electrical infrastructure products; inclusion should depend on whether data-center demand is material enough to offset pricing, litigation, and non-AI cyclicality.

This pass did not expand nuclear fuel, turbine OEMs, utilities, IPPs, or transformer-only suppliers due to the four-candidate limit; future Layer 1B passes should separately map HALEU/enrichment, turbine backlogs, and transformer components.

summary: Expanded the universe around the AI/data-center power bottleneck toward second-order electrical infrastructure suppliers and contractors rather than hyperscalers or mega-cap utilities. The strongest near-node evidence appears in medium-voltage switchgear, custom engineered data-center electrical solutions, electrical construction, T&D/substation work, and conduit/electrical infrastructure products. This pass intentionally favors less obvious public-market mappings over the already-visible cloud, GPU, nuclear, and utility reference names.
